AGENDA
  YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Tuesday, March 23, 2021
  6:30 P.M.
  The three-fold mission of the Youth & Family Action Committee is:
  1. To support positive activities and opportunities for young people;
  2. To strengthen families; and
  3. To combat the problems of substance abuse.

Tonight’s meeting will be held virtually in compliance with Governor Newson’s Executive
Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus. The meeting will be live streamed on
the La Verne You Tube channel at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream.

To make a comment on an agenda item or under public comment, email your phone
number to cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org. This email address will be monitored live during the
meeting and interested parties will be called. Please be aware there is a delay in the live
stream service and any requests to speak should be submitted as soon as possible.

LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  March23,2021

L A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Don Kendrick at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present (virtually):
  Executive Board
  Robin Carder, Chair - Mayor Pro Tem
  Rick Crosby, Vice Chair - Council Member
  Krista Chakmak, BUSD Board Member
  Carolyn Cockrell, Roynon Elementary School Counselor
  Denise Fisher, Resident

  Don Kendrick, Resident
  Donna Redman, Resident
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Kim Braswell, BUSD
  Cory Leeper, LVPD
  Janessa Gonzalez, LVPD
  Jessica Vozella, American Lung Association
  Gamaliel Polanco, Tri-City Mental Health
  Michelle Robinson, Tri-City Mental Health
  JR Ranells, City of La Verne

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the February 23,2021, meeting were
  approved.

4. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer (SRO) Janessa Gonzalez
  reported that she was back on campus and eagerly
  anticipating students coming back in the near future.
  Elementary students would be returning on a hybrid
  schedule as of April Sth with middle and high school
  students returning on April 12th. SRO Gonzalez
  noted that as a follow up to the last meeting
  regarding tobacco enforcement of a business in old
  town, an inspection was completed and the business
  was in compliance with applicable regulations. Vice-
  Chair Crosby inquired about if there would be an
  additional police presenc,e at schools the first week
  similar to previous years and SRO Gonzalez
  confirmed there would be.

  It was also noted that the school year would not be
  extended past the original end date.
 Youth & Family Action Commiftee Minutes March 23,2021, page 2

5. Youth Mental Health  Gamaliel Polanco with Tri-City Mental Health noted
  some recent staffing changes and introduced
  Michelle Robinson who is overseeing the School
  Counseling Program. Michelle shared information
  about herself as well as a report on the program.
  Michelle noted that the referrals have involved issues
  related to COVID-19 such as anxiety, inability to
  concentrate, not logging in remotely to classes, and
  confidence in social skills. New this year, the
  program has been connecting directly with families
  and this has been a successful transition, providing
  additional benefits through the program as well as
  connecting those in need to services.

  The group also discussed the benefit of the SRO
  program and the partnership with Tri-City Mental
  Health as well as the connection to homeless issues
  in the community.

6. BUSD In-Class Return  Mark Rodgers with the Bonita Unified School District
  (BUSD) shared information on the district plans to
  open on campus hybrid learning for elementary and
  other students based on state and county guidelines.
  Mark detailed the comprehensive planning process
  that has been taking place in preparation for the
  transition. Mark also noted the benefits of the BUSD's
  approach including its flexibility as restrictions change.
  The group also received information on lessons
  learned from other school districts that have previously
  opened. Mark also informed the group about the
  BUSD's plan to address learning loss at all levels.

  The group discussed the transition as well as
  celebrated some of the extracurricular activities
  returning under the appropriate guidelines.

7. Teen Center  JR Ranells with the City of La Veme provided an
  update on the proposed Teen Center at Las Flores
  Park. JR provided the group with information on the
  grant that was submitted to the state as well as
  information on the opposition to the Las Flores
  location. Vice Chair Crosby noted that he would like
  YFAC to put forth a letter of support of the Teen
  Center because of the benefits to the community. The
  group discussed the Teen Center and history of
  identifoing the Las Flores location. Member Cockrell
  requested additional information and it was agreed to
  follow up with the specifics of the updated
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes March 23,2021, page 3

  location/design features at a future meeting. Member
  Cockrell also noted her desire to incorporate all sides
  and address concerns raised with the project. JR
  shared fu(her information on the final location/design.

  The Executive Board voted to direct staff to draft a
  letter of support for the Teen Center and its location at
  Las Flores Park and send to both the City Council as
  well as the state division reviewing the grant proposal.

8. Public Comment  Peter (no last name given) gave his compliments to
  YFAC for their efforts with youth mental health. Peter
  also provided information on the opposition to the
  Teen Center project at Las Flores Park including but
  not limited to preserving green space. Peter
  requested that the City explore other altematives to
  locating the Teen Center at Las Flores Park.

  Two emails were received regarding the Teen Center
  (see attached)

  Jessica Vozella with the American Lung Association
  gave compliments to the group and its efforts in the
  community.

  Kimberly Braswell with Ramona Middle School shared
  her appreciation for the teachers, staff, and BUSD for
  their work with addressing concerns and challenges
  related to COVID-19 and bringing students back to
  campus.

9. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled lor April2T ,
  2021, at 6:30 p.m.

10. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:30 p.m

Respectfully subm itted,

JR Ranells
Assistant to the City Manager
 JR Ranells
